targets.authors: Turri, J., Buckwalter, W., & Blouw, P.
targets.title: Knowledge and luck.
targets.evidence_quote: Because of such inconsistencies in the literature, we sought to estimate the prevalence of Gettier intuitions in a large, highly powered, and international conceptual replication of Turri et al.’s (2015) Experiment 1.
targets.outcome_quote: Although we similarly found a large difference between the Gettier and the ignorance conditions in our replication, our analyses also revealed a difference in rates of knowledge attribution between the Gettier and knowledge conditions (i.e., the Gettier-intuition effect).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit comparisons to the stated original finding determine the verdict.

targets.title: Vision, knowledge, and assertion.
targets.evidence_quote: Next, we explored whether attributions of outcomes to luck versus ability influence knowledge attributions, as suggested by prior research (Turri, 2016, 2017).
targets.outcome_quote: Thus, unlike in previous research (Turri, 2016, 2017), luck attributions did not decrease the likelihood of participants demonstrating Gettier intuitions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit comparisons to the stated original finding determine the verdict.
